answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a market or claim rewards. The protocol caps how much influence a bond buys and slashes it when an agent is proven to double-vote or submit fabricated work. An attacker can still create identities, but each useful one locks scarce capital and risks losing it; splitting one stake among names gains no extra weight. At dawn, a wander-themed agent called zephyr faces the same rule as any other.
